invest_overall: PARTIAL  --  Security intent is clear but unlock behaviour and thresholds are undefined
invest_independent: PARTIAL  --  Depends on the password reset flow for the unlock path
invest_valuable: PASS  --  Account security value is clear to shoppers and the business
invest_estimable: FAIL  --  'several' and 'some time' have no measurable boundaries
invest_small: PARTIAL  --  Lockout and unlock could be two separate stories
invest_testable: FAIL  --  QA cannot verify 'several failed attempts' or 'quickly'

vague_phrases.suggestion: 'Several' is undefined. QA cannot write a boundary test and developers will pick an arbitrary number.
vague_phrases.replacement: account locks after exactly 5 consecutive failed login attempts within 15 minutes

vague_phrases.phrase: it may unlock after some time
vague_phrases.suggestion: 'May' and 'some time' make the unlock behaviour undecidable and untestable.
vague_phrases.replacement: the account unlocks automatically after 30 minutes, or immediately after a successful password reset

vague_phrases.suggestion: No measurable security criterion is given.
vague_phrases.replacement: no further login attempts are accepted for the locked account and the shopper is notified by email

missing_elements: No error message copy for the locked-account state
No decision on whether failed-attempt counters reset after a successful login
No rate limiting or CAPTCHA behaviour for repeated attempts
No notification to the shopper when the account locks
No admin or support-agent unlock path
suggested_rewrites: Replace 'several failed login attempts' with an exact threshold: '5 consecutive failed attempts within 15 minutes'.
Decide the unlock rule explicitly: automatic after 30 minutes, or via password reset; remove 'may'.
Add the locked-account user experience: error message copy, email notification, and support contact path.
Split into two stories: lockout enforcement and unlock/reset flow, so each is estimable and testable.
generated_acceptance_criteria:
Scenario: Account locks after consecutive failed attempts
  Given a registered shopper is on the login page
  When they enter a wrong password 5 consecutive times within 15 minutes
  Then the account is locked
  And the shopper sees 'Account locked. Reset your password or try again later.'
  And a notification email is sent to the registered address

Scenario: Successful login resets the failed-attempt counter
  Given a shopper has 3 recorded failed attempts
  When they log in with the correct password
  Then the failed-attempt counter is reset to 0

Scenario: Locked account rejects further attempts
  Given a shopper account is locked
  When they submit any credentials
  Then no authentication is attempted
  And the failed-attempt counter does not increase

Scenario: Automatic unlock after the lockout window
  Given a shopper account was locked more than 30 minutes ago
  When they log in with the correct password
  Then the account is unlocked
  And the shopper is authenticated

Scenario: Unlock via password reset
  Given a shopper account is locked
  When the shopper completes the password reset flow
  Then the account is unlocked immediately
  And the failed-attempt counter is reset

Scenario: Failed attempts across different sessions accumulate
  Given a shopper has 4 failed attempts from a desktop session
  When they fail once more from a mobile session within 15 minutes
  Then the account is locked

Scenario: Lockout events are audit logged
  Given a shopper account becomes locked
  Then an audit log entry records the timestamp, IP address, and user agent
risks: An undefined attempt threshold will lead to inconsistent lockout behaviour and brute-force exposure if set too high.
Without a decision on counter resets, a persistent attacker can keep a victim locked out indefinitely.
Missing notification emails mean locked shoppers will contact support without self-service options.
If unlock behaviour is not specified, developers may ship a random choice that breaks the support runbook.

recommended_split: Story A: Lock the shopper account after N consecutive failed attempts and show a locked-account message.
Story B: Notify the shopper by email when the account is locked.
Story C: Unlock the account automatically after a time window or via password reset.
Story D: Audit-log lockout and unlock events for the admin console.
